name: Brownish Grey
lede: Brownish grey is a plain descriptive name for a grey with some brown in it, and it has been used in color lists for two centuries.

sections.title: A name that describes
sections.body: Brownish grey is two ordinary words used as a color name, and the dictionary of colour keeps several older names that mean the same thing [1]. *Fuscous* is defined as brown, dingy and dark, and also as a brownish grey [1][2]. [[taupe]], French for "mole", is also brownish grey, and its first record as a color word is 1911 [3]. Limestone and the butter-nut tree are each described as brownish grey, and ash can mean either whitish grey or brownish grey [4][5]. In 1923 a newspaper used *castor* for a dark brownish grey or light brown, the color of beaver fur [6].

sections.title: In the old grey series
sections.body: The phrase appears in the grey series of a color nomenclature reproduced in a book on nature's palette, between reddish grey and greyish black [7]. In that order grey passes through bluish, greenish and yellowish variants before the reddish and brownish ones [7]. These are shades of [[grey]] that lean toward [[brown]] [7].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 calls this swatch "grayish yellowish brown", about 5 units of color difference away [8]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 records the name from 1926 [8]. Compare [[greyish-brownish-olive]], a darker neighbor, and plain [[grey]] [8].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The ColorHub archive files this color with the browns; its lightness is about 51 out of 100 and its chroma is low, 15 [8]. Contrast against white is 4.36 to 1, enough for large text [8].

origin.first_recorded: in a Werner-type grey series; Maerz and Paul record 1926
origin.source: Baty, Nature's Palette; Maerz and Paul via ColorHub
